LETTER514
Tunable 1,3-Lithium Shift of Propargylic/Allenylic Lithiums Formed by 
Conjugate Addition of 4-Aryl-3-butyn-1-enes with Organolithiums and the 
Subsequent Transmetalation/Pd(0)-Catalyzed Coupling Reaction with Aryl 
Halides
Tunable 1,3-Lithium Shift of Propargylic/Allenylic LithiumsShengming Ma,* Qiwen He, Xin Jin
State Key Laboratory of Organometallic Chemistry, Shanghai Institute of Organic Chemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences, 
354 Fenglin Lu, Shanghai 200032, P. R. China
Fax +86(21)64167510; E-mail: masm@mail.sioc.ac.cn
Received 5 November 2004
SYNLETT 2005, No. 3, pp 0514–051616 .02 .20 05
Advanced online publication: 17.01.2005
DOI: 10.1055/s-2005-862349; Art ID: U30804ST
© Georg Thieme Verlag Stuttgart · New York
Abstract: A protocol was established to control the 1,3-lithium
shift in propargylic/allenylic species formed by the conjugate addi-
tion of 4-aryl-3-butyn-1-enes with organolithiums. Subsequent
transmetalation and Pd(0)-catalyzed cross-coupling with aryl ha-
lides afforded 1,1-diarylallenes and 1,3-diarylallenes, respectively,
the structural diversities of which are determined by the easily
availability of both 4-aryl-3-butyn-1-enes and the organolithium re-
agents.
Key words: conjugated enynes, organolithiums, conjugate addi-
tion, Negishi coupling, allenes
Allenes, a class of compounds possessing two cumulative
carbon-carbon double bonds, have aroused much atten-
tion due to its unique reactivity in organic synthesis.
1,2
One challenge is to make allenes with a high selectivity.3,4
Recently, we reported a controlled 1,3-lithium shift reac-
tion of propargylic/allenylic lithiums, which was followed
by sequential transmetalation and Pd(0)-catalyzed cross-
coupling with aryl halids to afford 1,1-diaryl allenes or
1,3-diaryl allenes highly selectively,
5 however, the scope
of this reaction is very limited in terms of the starting
alkynes. In this paper we wish to report a new protocol
controlling the 1,3-lithium shift in propargylic/allenylic
species formed by the conjugate addition of 4-aryl-3-bu-
tyn-1-enes with organolithiums.
6 Subsequent transmetal-
lation and Pd(0)-catalyzed cross-coupling with aryl
halides afforded 1,1-diarylallenes and 1,3-diarylallenes,
respectively (Scheme 1).
We initially tested the effect of temperature on carbolithi-
ation, which led to the conclusion that lower carbolithia-
tion temperature (T
1) favors the formation of 1,1-
diphenylocta-1,2-diene 1a while higher carbolithiation
temperature favors the formation of 1,3-diphenylocta-1,2-
diene 2a (Scheme 2). However, although the ratios of the
two products can be tuned by conducting the carbolithia-
tion at different temperature, the yields were lower when
the reactions were carried out at a higher temperature.

Furthermore some additives were tested for the 1,3-lithi-
um shift reaction: (1) pyridine, n-Bu4NI, N,N-diisopropyl-
ethylamine and DMAP have little effect on the 1,3-
lithium shift. (2) Although TMEDA has some interesting
effect,
5 the reaction was not easily reproducible. (3)
Through trial and error, we finally established a set of re-
producible conditions to realize a clean 1,3-lithium shift.
After 4-phenyl-3-butyn-1-ene was carbolithiated with n-
BuLi at –78 °C for one hour, we added HMPA (2 equiv)
at –78 °C, which was followed by warming up to room
temperature naturally, subsequent transmetallation and
Pd(0)-catalyzed cross-coupling led to the exclusive for-
mation of 2a in 83% yield, indicating a complete 1,3-lith-
ium shift (Table 1, entry 2).
Thus, different conditions were established for the highly
selective formation of 1,1-diarylallenes 1 or 1,3-diarylal-
lenes 2. Conditions A affording 1,1-diarylallenes 1: 4-
phenyl-3-butyn-1-ene was carbolithiated with n-BuLi at –
78 °C for 1 hour, followed by transmetallation and cou-
pling at room temperature. Conditions B: 4-phenyl-3-bu-
tyn-1-ene was carbolithiated with n-BuLi at –78 °C for 1
hour, followed by additon of HMPA (2 equiv) at –78 °C,
then warming up to room temperature naturally. Subse-
quent transmetallation and Pd(0)-catalyzed coupling reac-
tion afforded 1,3-lithium shift product 2.
Some typical results are summarized in Table 1, indicat-
ing that: (1) 1° through 3° organolithium reagents could
be used; (2) these two sets of reaction conditions are

general for differently substituted 4-aryl-3-butyn-1-enes
and aryl halides; (3) the yields of the reactions are from
good to excellent.
The reaction of 4-phenyl-2-methyl-3-butyn-1-ene used
both conditions A and B afforded only 1,1-diphenylallene
3a, indicating the importance of the proton at the 2-posi-
tion of the starting material for the 1,3-lithium shift
(Scheme 3).
In conclusion, we have developed a convenient method to
control the 1,3-lithium shift in propargylic/allenylic spe-
cies in situ formed by the conjugate addition of 4-aryl-3-
butyn-1-ene with organolithium reagents in an excellent
selectivity. Due to the easily availability and structural di-
versities of both starting compounds, this method will be
very useful for the selective synthesis of allenes. Further
studies on the scope and mechanism of this methodology
are being carried out in our laboratory.
